text: Raid day. Black Hound has turned a B-grade gate into a press event.
For the cameras, Mok hugs the man he locked in with a boss.
Through his grin, Mok promises a last photo. Jaeha has had one memorial already.
Jaeha's smile doesn't move. Mok isn't the only one here with a plan.
A hundred and fifty thousand watch Bomi's stream, and not everyone buys the friendship.
Mok has kept Bomi out, for her own good, meaning no witnesses. She has found the loophole.
Sora strolls by with a wink, teasing him about his drowsy husks. The drowsiness is deliberate.
Her compass snaps to summons in field form. At rest, Nib and Borro barely stir it.
Three hunters by the van carry cables and a steel stake, and they'll go in last.
Jaeha knows that double hexagon from the secret gate under the bridge. Kanghan gear, on Mok's raid.
Inside: the drowned cathedral Sora described, knee-deep water and silent bronze bells. Jaeha wades in first, chalk in hand.
Mok planned for two summons. At the edge of Jaeha's vision, a held call says otherwise.
Two hunters snigger at his back. Twenty million views, and he's still their trap rat.
Jaeha flings out an arm. A blade swings from a pillar, right where his next step would land.
He chalks a neat cross beside it, the trap-tester's sign for keep away.
Mok waves everyone on. A trap-tester is worth every won, right up until the boss room.
It's the code on the notebook's first pages, in Minseok's hand, and Mok's men trust it blindly.
A junction: one way onward, one down into a flooded crypt, one dead end.
Jaeha chalks a safe-way arrow pointing down into the drowned crypt, with one tiny extra tick.
Then, with a perfectly blank face, he takes the middle passage.
Yerin caught it. Jaeha only smiles. That sign isn't meant for his own team.
After that, the marks are honest: arrow after arrow, down the aisle.
Under a bronze bell green with age, Nib stops dead, ears flat.
A bell rang the retreat that left Nib alone on the Ninth Wall. Jaeha needs no explanation.
Sora's needle is still slack.
Sora looks from the dead needle to the stiff husks and sees the trick. She's enjoying it.
Next, a side nave with a dry, tiled floor. Jaeha stops at the threshold.
Jaeha politely warns that a dry floor in a flooded cathedral is wrong. Mok doesn't turn round.
A hunter's boot presses a dark tile. Click.
Both pairs of doors slam at once, trapping the whole raid between them, Jaeha's team too.
Water blasts from grates high in the walls, and it's rising fast.
Two hunters haul at the doors. They don't move an inch.
Only Borro's field form could force those doors, and Sora's compass is watching. The secret, or their lives.
He chooses their lives, even Mok's. One squeeze, and green flares behind Borro's husk face.
Across the nave, the needle snaps round to Borro and blazes.
Borro wedges his shield into the crack and heaves. The doors part, and the flood pours out.
Jaeha clings to a pillar, carrying sixty percent of the strain, his nose bleeding.
He waves them all through, every hunter who sneered at his back, one by one.
A young hunter gapes at the green eyes behind the husk face. Husks don't save anyone. Borro does.
Mok shoves through, furious at being saved by a husk. Sora greets her needle like an old friend.
Borro steps out last, the green fading, and the doors grind shut.
Jaeha wipes his nose, oddly calm. A watcher who thinks she has it all stops looking.
The soaked hunters can't look at Borro. One bows his head, without a word.
Mok can't have his men bowing to a husk. It's a tool, he barks. It follows orders.
Next, a narrow ledge above the flooded nave, bells at arm's reach. Sora walks at the back.
A carved trigger beside the ledge, already marked with a cross. A heavy bell hangs above it.
Sora lifts her crossbow, as if adjusting her grip, and aims past the line.
Her bolt hits the trigger. The bell drops straight at Jaeha's head.
One calm step aside, and it crashes past his shoulder. His husks don't twitch.
It hits the water far below, and one deep toll booms through the cathedral.
Sora's needle stays slack. That was the test: put him in danger, wait for a summon to wake.
Jaeha bows like a shop clerk: that trap was marked. Sora laughs it off. Nobody's fooled.
The raid rests in a dry chapel, Mok huddled with the sealers. Nib is nowhere to be seen.
Jaeha seems to doze. Through the link, he sees a narrow crack behind the altar, and moving air.
Nib slips back with cobwebs on his ears, as if he never left. He found what Jaeha wanted.
Jaeha doesn't even open his eyes. Only the corner of his mouth lifts.
Yerin watched Mok lock them in with a boss once. She's sure he'll do it twice. Jaeha sounds pleased.
He gives her chalk and orders for when the door shuts. The healer who froze before a lizard is past that.
In his earpiece, Bomi reports: her drone sneaked in, four hundred and ten thousand watching. It needs a hiding place.
The one place no hunter looks: the drone nests in Borro's moss, its lens peeking between the flowers.
At the nave's end: tall bronze doors under a rose window, and a silent bell.
And a lamp above the doors, burning red. The grade is wrong again.
Mok heaves a door open and bows toward the dark, a host showing a guest to his seat.
Jaeha smiles up at the red lamp and hands Mok's own rule back, word for word.
Jaeha, Nib, Borro and Yerin wade into a dark round chamber, something huge slumped in the middle.
The doors swing shut. In the last strip of red light, Mok smiles as a sealer raises the stake.
Jaeha watches the gap close without a flicker. Mok shut the door on cue. For once, that's the plan.
